headline: U.S. Federal Reserve Raises Rates to 3.75%–4.00%, Signals More Tightening May Follow
seoTitle: U.S. Fed Raises Rates to 3.75%–4.00% | FMB News
seoDescription: The U.S. Federal Reserve raised its benchmark target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00% on September 16, its first increase in more than three years.
deck: The Federal Reserve unanimously raised its benchmark rate by a quarter percentage point as it said U.S. inflation remains elevated. The move matters beyond the United States because dollar interest rates influence currencies, borrowing costs and capital flows globally, including in the Philippines.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00% at its September 16 meeting. The decision was unanimous.
Reuters reported that this was the Federal Reserve's first interest-rate increase in more than three years and that policymakers flagged the possibility of additional tightening in coming months.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: The Federal Reserve's published statement says economic activity is expanding at a solid pace but inflation remains elevated. The central bank said the increase is intended to support a timelier return to its 2% inflation goal.
The implementation note makes the new target effective September 17 and raises the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 3.90% and the primary credit rate to 4.00%.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The move reverses the direction of the Fed's most recent easing cycle. Reuters reported that policymakers' September projections point to another increase this year, although future decisions remain subject to economic data and are not guaranteed.

Reuters also reported that global shares moved modestly higher on Thursday while the U.S. dollar held near a seven-week high after the decision. Market movements can change rapidly and should not be read as a definitive judgment on the policy decision.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipino readers
paragraphs: U.S. monetary policy can affect the dollar, global bond yields, cross-border capital flows and financing conditions. Those channels can in turn influence Philippine financial markets, the peso and borrowing conditions, although the scale and direction of any Philippine effect depend on domestic conditions and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas policy as well as global developments.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch incoming U.S. inflation and labor data, the Federal Reserve's October meeting, movements in the dollar and Treasury yields, and how Asian central banks and markets respond. Any further rate move will be reported as a separate development only when confirmed.
